summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Frank Rush, a coal miner lodging over Tom Allen's saloon at 621 Market Street, was shot outside it by a stranger who escaped; Allen and others suspected revenge for an earlier ejection.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Monday, December 22, 1884, page 5. article.json has no focus field.

facts.fact: Allen's saloon, the Champion's Rest, was at 621 Market Street, with free and easy concerts given nightly
places: Champion's Rest, 621 Market Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Frank Rush, a coal miner who lodged over Allen's saloon, was shot in front of it at 1 a.m. by an unknown man who escaped
Allen described the shooting to the paper
facts.quote: It wasn't half a minute before we heard the shots as fast as a man could fire a gun. When we got outside the man was gone.
